doc.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20

title: Kid Twat Butler: the Boudoir nickname and birth
summary: Butler explains his cigarette-testing nickname and gives his 1907 Christmas birthday, mentioning hearing Louis Armstrong at about ten.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: See? What are they calling you now? It's from the Boudoir. It has to be from the Boudoir. That's my handle. That's the handle you put on that. Well, the Boudoir, you see, I'm going to show you a lot of people don't know what a Boudoir is. You see, when I came down here from Memphis, you see, and I was cigarette test up there, and you go in there and smoke and test them cigarettes. That's what you call a Boudoir. What kind of cigarettes?

Just to feel. Oh, you're kidding me. Yeah, well, I came down here at, of course, I'm speaking about Chesterfields. Now, I'm not talking about my life here. I ain't got to that yet. Well, this is my home, but that's how I made my living. And so now one cigarette ain't more than the other one with me. Now, because I done tried them all from Cooper on the Black Cat, you know, so he's smoky, but he's smoke, you know. Well, where were you born?
In Algea's, Louisiana. In Algea's, Louisiana.
And do you mind telling me what year and the date exactly?

The date exactly? 1907 on the 25th of December. I have my birthday with Jesus Christ. That's why I'm a lucky boy. So nobody that makes me don't get nothing on birthday anymore than what I'm supposed to get eaten and things like that. That's everybody that has that day, you know. So, well, that's speaking and going on. I'm not talking about music and things like that. Well, I've been around, you know what I mean? I've been around. And Louis Armstrong, I was a very young kid. Of course, when I started bass, I was, I guess I must have been about 10 years old. And Fowlin' Louis Armstrong and, oh, Tailgate Wagon, Buddy P.T. and all them cats like that. Excuse me. When they have to go and, oh, we just as sad going to the graveyard, you know. And when we coming back, well, we tear them up. We forget about them just that quick. We done put them away, you know.
